title: Inspired Word of God
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child explains why the Bible is the inspired word of God (2 Timothy 3:16-17: God-breathed; useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness) and names three of its writers (Moses, David, Paul).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the Bible has an Old and New Testament.
floor.question: How many books are in the New Testament?

board.say: What does it tell us about who is behind the Bible?

board.do: Wait for the child to say God inspired the writers.

listen_for: One person wrote all of it
misconceptions.ask: How many authors does the Bible have?
misconceptions.repair: Show the contents page: many books, written over many years by many writers, all inspired by God.

listen_for: It is only the ideas of wise men
misconceptions.ask: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 say about Scripture?
misconceptions.repair: Read 2 Timothy 3:16: "God-breathed". People wrote, God inspired.

misconceptions.ask: What is Scripture useful for (2 Timothy 3:16)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 2 Timothy 3:16-17 and list its four uses: teaching, rebuking, correcting, training in righteousness.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these wrote books of the Bible?
misconceptions.repair: Match writers to books: Moses (the Law, by tradition), David (many Psalms), Paul (letters). Jesus' words were written down by the Gospel writers.

checks.question: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 say about Scripture?
Name one writer of the Bible.

skills.key_step: The child discusses why the Bible was translated into local languages (so people understand it in their own language, so the message reaches every home) and outlines advantages (understanding, more readers, growth of faith, the language is honoured).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the Bible is God's inspired word.
floor.question: What does God-breathed mean?

representations: one verse in English, Kiswahili and a local language
steps: Ask: is the message the same?
contexts: a grandmother reading a Kikamba Bible

board.do: Write John 3:16 in English and in Kiswahili side by side.

board.say: Is the message the same or different?

board.do: Wait for the child to say the same.

listen_for: Yes, it makes a new message
misconceptions.ask: Does translating the Bible change its message?
misconceptions.repair: Show one verse in English, Kiswahili and a local language: same meaning, different words.

listen_for: There is no need: English is enough for everyone
misconceptions.ask: Why translate the Bible into local languages?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: if a grandmother reads only Dholuo, how will she hear God's word? Translation lets everyone understand.

misconceptions.ask: Which is an advantage of reading the Bible in your own language?
misconceptions.repair: List real advantages: understanding, more readers, the message reaches homes, faith grows in one's own language.

misconceptions.ask: When the Bible is translated into Kikuyu, what happens to its books?
misconceptions.repair: Compare contents pages of an English and a Kiswahili Bible: the same books in the same order.

checks.question: Does translation change the Bible's message?
checks.answer: No: the same message in another language

checks.question: Name an advantage of a Bible in your own language.
